title: Inclusive European Heritage Residency 2026 in Malta: peer learning in practice
content:
From 13 to 19 September, Malta’s rich cultural heritage took centre stage during the second Inclusive European Heritage Residency, bringing together 10 selected participants from across Europe for peer learning activities and exchanges with dozens of volunteers and professionals from Din l-Art Helwa – the National Trust for Malta, as well as professionals from Europa Nostra and INTO.

The Residency aimed to strengthen the capacity and connections of heritage organisations across Europe, supporting more inclusive, sustainable and community-led approaches to heritage protection. The Residency was organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union.

title: European experts call for immediate Grade 1 protection and adaptive reuse of British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Malta
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the preservation of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray in Gozo, Malta. An exceptionally important element of Gozo’s architectural, social and European heritage, the Barracks were constructed at the turn of the 20th century as married quarters for British military families, and are now threatened with demolition to make way for a new five-storey spa hotel, which would incorporate only a reconstructed version of the historic arcaded façade.

The British Barracks at Fort Chambray were listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2026, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Din l-Art Ħelwa – the National Trust for Malta.

The European experts recommend protecting the British Barracks through Grade 1 scheduling and pursuing their adaptive reuse, arguing that conservation and economic development can be mutually supportive and that the building can contribute to the future sustainable development of Fort Chambray and Gozo.

title: British-Turkish novelist and storyteller Elif Shafak wins Helena Vaz da Silva European Award 2026
content:
Press release English – Portuguese

The acclaimed British-Turkish author Elif Shafak is the winner of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness on Cultural Heritage 2026. This European recognition pays tribute to Elif Shafak’s exceptional ability to bring Europe’s rich and diverse cultural heritage to life through her captivating storytelling, while responding to the challenges of our time with a powerful call for defending democracy, promoting solidarity, embracing cosmopolitanism and celebrating cultural diversity.

Elif Shafak – Photo credit: Ferhat Elik

The Helena Vaz da Silva European Award was established in 2013 by the Centro Nacional de Cultura (Portugal) in collaboration with Europa Nostra and the Portuguese Press Club, and has the support of the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Portugal, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and Tourism of Portugal.

The award ceremony will take place on 5 November at the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.
creator: Joana Pinheiro

title: Cross-border community in action: How the Historic Centre of Stolberg (Germany) came back to life
content:
After a mass flood in mid-July 2021 devastated the Historic Centre of Stolberg in the western part of Germany, causing severe damage to hundreds of buildings, the centre of the 500-year-old town was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2022. Since its involvement in the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra, the Historic Centre of Stolberg  has not only been successfully rebuilt, but strengthened its network and community in the process — a completely unexpected, and very welcome outcome of the selection. Europa Nostra sat down with Dr. Karl Schmeer, Chemist and Biologist, who was involved in the nomination of the site for the 7 Most Endangered Programme, to hear about the Historic Centre of Stolberg’s inspiring journey.

It was a bad situation, the Historic Centre of Stolberg was badly flooded. It happened at an unexpected time. It was mid-July, and it had been raining for six weeks, when suddenly two meters of water flooded the main streets. It was dangerous and rough. This was a wakeup call, everyone’s talking about climate change and the effects and now we saw it. Two days later, the city centre was devastated.

title: Europa Nostra has strategic meeting with Assistant Director-General for Culture at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris
content:
On 16 September 2026, Europa Nostra had an excellent first meeting with Nayef H. Al-fayez, UNESCO Assistant Director-General for Culture, at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, France. Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović and Board Member Laurent Lévi-Strauss, himself a former high-official of UNESCO, represented Europa Nostra at this strategic meeting.

The discussion focused on the centrality of culture and cultural heritage for peace, climate action and the overall resilience of our shared humanity. To champion this strategic goal, we need an even stronger partnership between UNESCO and the European Union, with the vital contribution of civil society.

Credit: Europa Nostra

title: Europa Nostra’s Letter to the President of the European Commission ahead of the State of the Union 2026
content:
Read/download the Letter in PDF

Dear Madam President of the European Commission,
Mrs Ursula von der Leyen

A few days ahead of your very important speech on the State of the European Union, we felt an urgency and a necessity to write to you in our capacity as Executive President and Secretary General of Europa Nostra, the largest organisation in Europe committed to the protection of Cultural Heritage, tangible and intangible, which is a long-standing civil society interlocutor and partner of the European Union.

First of all, we would like to reiterate our congratulations to you for two recent major EU policy documents, namely the Culture Compass for Europe and the Joint Declaration which you co-signed with the Presidents of the European Parliament and the Council of the EU under the motto “Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe”. We consider these two documents as crucial milestones for the European Union in a world marked by violence and polarisation, as well as by uncertainty and anxiety.

title: European experts call for protection of Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex in Gothenburg, Sweden, under threat of demolition
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the future of the Valhalla Swimming Hall Complex (Valhallabadet) in Gothenburg, Sweden. Open seven days a week and welcoming around 500,000 visitors annually, Valhallabadet is one of Gothenburg’s most important public swimming facilities, yet it is under threat due to plans to demolish it to make way for an expanded events area. Its modernist architectural design, including its outstanding abstract mosaics covering the halls, received the Bronze Medal for Architectural Design at the 1948 Olympic Games.

The complex was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2025, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Europa Nostra Sweden.

title: 7 Most Endangered Programme 2027: Call for nominations now open
content:
Across Europe, our shared cultural heritage is under threat: from disasters caused by natural and human-induced hazards to the impacts of climate-change, conflict, neglect, poorly planned development, violation of the rule of law and lack of funding.

If you know of endangered heritage in your country, nominate it for the next edition of the 7 Most Endangered Programme by 23 October 2026.

The 7 Most Endangered Programme is run by Europa Nostra – the leading European heritage civil society network – which is supported by the European Investment Bank (EIB) Institute and also by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union.

Since its launch in 2013, the 7 Most Endangered Programme has become a key European civil society initiative dedicated to safeguarding Europe’s endangered heritage. Over more than a decade, the Programme has highlighted 77 endangered heritage sites in 35 countries.

Each year, the Programme selects seven heritage sites at risk and brings together heritage and financial expertise, public authorities, owners and custodians, civil society organisations and local communities to help develop viable pathways for their long-term safeguarding.

title: Europa Nostra participates in the panel hike “How to Leverage Europe’s Strengths” at the European Forum Alpbach 2026, Austria
content:
Europa Nostra’s Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović participated in the European Forum Alpbach 2026 held in the Tyrolean village of Alpbach, Austria, under the theme “How Europe Wins”. On 2 September, she took part in the panel “Hike | A Bunch of (Hidden) Champions – How to Leverage Europe’s Strengths”, together with Sandra Navidi, CEO of Beyond Global, and Arnold Kammel, Secretary General of the Austrian Federal Ministry of Defence (BMLV). The discussion was moderated by Cathryn Clüver Ashbrook, Executive Vice-President of Bertelsmann Stiftung.

Europe is home to global market leaders, world-class research, the rule of law and human rights – set against a rich backdrop of intellectual history, philosophy, culture, heritage and art. The panelist explored how these assets can be harnessed to strengthen European resilience and security in the face of geopolitical upheaval.

Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović highlighted how the rule of law, democracy and human rights can be understood as endangered forms of intangible cultural heritage, and stressed the importance of defending these fundamental European values.

title: Europa Nostra awards Maestro Plácido Domingo its highest honour for championing Europe’s cultural heritage
content:
Press release in English | Italian | Spanish

Brussels / Torre del Lago, 31 August 2026

Europa Nostra – the leading European heritage civil society organisation – granted its Medal of Honour to Plácido Domingo, world-renowned opera singer and conductor, who presided over Europa Nostra for a decade (2010-2020). This recognition honours both his exceptional service at the helm of the organisation and his immense dedication to promoting Europe’s cultural heritage. Plácido Domingo received the Europa Nostra Medal of Honour yesterday evening on stage at the Gran Teatro all’Aperto Giacomo Puccini in Torre del Lago, Italy, at the end of his Gala concert held within the framework of this year’s Puccini Festival.
